## What was tried

**The problem.** Today the owner and every AI helper that works for the owner (the Orca coordinator and worker sessions, scripts, the pull-request helper) sign in to GitHub as the same user, `ironbelly`, which is also the repository admin. GitHub cannot tell who did something: the person clicking "Approve" or a script running on the same machine. Our own checks cannot tell either.

**Why it matters.** The plan says things like "a worker cannot merge", "an approval means the owner approved", "a typed go means the owner typed it". On a shared login these rules can be written down but not proven. The plan already records this as open risks (requirement SEC-09, risk RK-3, invariant INV-025 in the unification plan). The plan's current default is: the typed-answer check cannot pass, so every merge is typed by hand.

**What was tried.** On 2026-11-22 two agents proposed and debated (three rounds) and a reconciler unified one proposal. The owner shelved it for further human debate and asked that the problem be filed with that proposal as one of the proposed solutions. Nothing below is decided or built.

**Proposed solutions (not decided).**

1. **Two tiers plus a separate agent GitHub account (the debated proposal).** "The owner" means the person behind `ironbelly`, by numeric id.
   - Tier 1, chat-only answers (a grant, a cleanup approval, a design go): counts only when the owner types it in a session the owner opened by hand; never from workers, script-started sessions, relays, or issue or PR text. Free, and can be done now. It narrows the risk but cannot prove who typed.
   - Tier 2, a merge or the `Approved` label: the chat go plus an approving GitHub review by the `ironbelly` account on that exact commit, clicked by the owner in the browser. The checks refuse if the login in use is the owner's own, or if no such review exists.
   - A second GitHub account for the agents (Write role, outside collaborator, 2FA), with `ironbelly` signed out of agent hosts. It must exist before merge automation, coordinator autostart, switching the watcher on for real repos, and flipping the worker-binding switch.
   - Needs the master protection rules (the ruleset of the plan's item OA-5) to make "a worker cannot merge" true.
2. **Chat-only rule, no new account.** Do only Tier 1. Cheap, but a script on the host can still type as the owner.
3. **Status quo.** Every merge is typed by hand by the owner; merge automation, coordinator autostart, real-repo watcher switch-on and the worker-binding flip stay off.
4. **Not evaluated yet:** a GitHub App (a bot identity) instead of a second user account.

**Costs (estimates, not measured).** Tier 1: about 15 minutes of the owner's time and about 1 agent hour. Second account: about 1 to 1.5 owner hours once, about 15 minutes per extra host, about 1 to 2 minutes per gated merge, plus about 3 to 4 agent hours of code and tests. Ruleset time belongs to OA-5.

**Risks of solution 1.** An `ironbelly` credential left on a host; the owner logging back in under pressure; review bots (Augment, Codex) staying silent on a new account, which reads as clean; credential expiry stopping all agents (fails safe); at 0 required approvals a worker could merge a path the rules do not gate.

**Unknowns.** Whether a Write-role account can do the claim's writes (assignee, issue type, Complexity field, `Approved` field); whether Augment and Codex review pull requests from a new account; how many hosts exist.

**Open choices from the debate.** (1) Required approvals on master: 1 (recommended by the debate, no agent self-merge on any path) or 0. (2) Should the agent account join the Coder organisation: no to start. (3) Reuse the existing `IB-AIReviewer` account: no, create a new one.

## Relevant files and links

- Plan items: OA-6 (who counts as "the owner"), OA-5 (master protection), OA-18, OA-19, OA-20 (all wait on this), SEC-09, RK-3, INV-025, decision D16 (review rule), `SPEC.md` lines 577 and 578. Local plan files, not pushed: `.dev/brainstorms/20261120-pr686-unify/`.
- The debate (local, not pushed): `.dev/brainstorms/20261122-owner-actions-debate/X05/` (`FINAL.md`, rounds A-0 to B-3).
- Related: issue 717 (watcher: real-repo switch-on and the worker-binding flip wait on this), issue 716 (coordinator).

## Done when

The owner records in chat which solution is chosen (or a new one). Then either the dependent items (merge automation, coordinator autostart, real-repo watcher switch-on, the worker-binding flip) are unblocked with the chosen mechanism built and tested, or they are confirmed to stay off. If solution 1 is chosen: the agent account exists and is cut over on one host, the throwaway tests in the debate file pass (the login prints the agent account in a fresh shell and in an Orca session; an unapproved agent PR cannot merge; `gh pr merge --admin` and a push to master are refused; both review bots review an agent-authored PR; the claim writes work).

## Pick-up note

Parked for human debate. Do not build anything yet. The owner decides whether any of this is wanted; there is no deadline. Read `X05/FINAL.md` for the full order of steps, the owner's one-sentence approval, and what an agent would do after it.

## Backlog review, 2026-11-24

Read-only review of this issue against the current source and its history (automated analysis, then an independent evidence review; the findings were corrected once after a first review failed and passed the second).

- **State:** still-relevant
- **Complexity / size:** Complex / L
- **Priority:** P1

#### Concrete next steps
1. No implementation is authorized. The coordinator should recover the missing debate and plan, check for a later owner decision, and present the choice to the owner in chat if it remains undecided. Do not infer not-planned from a parked proposal.
2. If the owner chooses to keep the privileged automation off, record that explicit choice and which dependent capabilities remain disabled. Verify their actual state before claiming the issue's completion condition is met.
3. Only if the owner chooses an automation-enabling solution, plan its minimum implementation and authorized one-host trial. For the separate-account proposal, #722 requires identity cutover, protection against an unapproved merge and direct master push, both reviewer bots on an agent-authored PR, and working claim writes. A GitHub App remains an unevaluated alternative, not an approved substitution. Do not run credential changes, denial probes, writes or activation from this review.
4. Re-run the independent review gate against this revision and its successful live reads before using this report to close or change any issue. The previous QA remains FAIL until that separate review occurs. There is no authorization to perform a GitHub write here.

#### Dependencies
- **Needs:** the owner's explicit solution decision. If an automation-enabling route is chosen, it also needs the master-protection work called OA-5 in #722 (repository protection rules); a distinct prerequisite issue number was not verified.
- **Blocks parts of [#716](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/716), the coordinator feature backlog:** privileged merge automation and coordinator autostart as identified by #722, not every coordinator feature.
- **Blocks parts of [#717](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/717), the watcher feature backlog:** real-repository switch-on and the worker-binding flip as identified by #722, not all watcher implementation. Neither whole backlog must close before the owner can choose a solution.
- The mapping from the local plan's stage labels to separately filed issues is **UNVERIFIED**, because the cited local plan is absent.

#### Related issues
- #716, coordinator feature backlog: directly mentioned by #722. Its live issue read was saved by the tool as a large result; full content was not needed to infer a whole-issue dependency and no such dependency is asserted.
- #717, watcher feature backlog: directly mentioned by #722. Its live body includes narrower-token work and session-permission checks, which are adjacent to this decision, not substitutes for it.
- Other numbered issues are not claimed as prerequisites or duplicates. No evidence read establishes that #722 duplicates a completed fix.

#### Related PRs
- [PR #686](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/pull/686), the original orchestrator-wake watcher proposal: referenced indirectly by the issue's plan-folder name. Live read returned CLOSED, `mergedAt: null`, `mergeCommit: null`; its 2026-11-23 closing comment says PR #707 is the merged watcher design. Its body and returned discussion were read. Closing #686 did not complete the separate identity decision in #722.
- [PR #707](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/pull/707), the zero-setup watcher and approval-field work: the revision's independent live read returned MERGED at 2026-11-20T22:09:24Z, with merge commit 2ea524514154bde03258a7d7d8a0265c371609af and no closing issue references. Its body describes watcher/approval-field work, not a chosen human-identity mechanism; returned comments and review summaries do not record a solution choice for #722. This supports #686's closing note, not completion of #722. Direct source and regression-test reads still show host-login approval acceptance. Inline review-thread contents were not returned by these reads and remain **UNVERIFIED**.
- No dedicated resolving PR for #722 was established. Bounded all-state PR searches (100-result limit each) for `722 in:title,body`, `"agent account" in:title,body` and `"host login" in:title,body` returned only unrelated PR #585 for the first query (its body mentions a document's line 722), and zero results for the other two. Neither #686 nor #707 has closing issue references. This is negative evidence from those searches only; PRs using other wording or linking #722 only in comments remain **UNVERIFIED**.

_Limits: the full GitHub event timeline could not be read in this review and is unverified. Nothing was changed on this issue other than this comment and its field values._

title: [FEATURE] The owner and the AI helpers share one GitHub login: decide how to tell who approved (a separate agent account is one proposed solution)
